entities.summary:
**Identity & Significance**: The Cat on a Hot Tin Roof is a stage play by Tennessee Williams, created around 1955. This dramatic work matters in the arc of world history as it exemplifies the existential crises and social tensions prevalent in post-war America.

**What Happened**: The core events surrounding this play revolve around Maggie 'Maggie's' desire for autonomy amidst her stifling relationships with her family members, particularly her brother Charles. This struggle is set against the backdrop of a Southern American setting where patriarchal norms are challenged by feminist undertones. Through its portrayal, Williams critiques societal expectations and explores themes of identity, morality, and the human condition.

**Legacy & Consequence**: The Cat on a Hot Tin Roof's influence can be seen in subsequent works that also probed the complexities of human relationships and social hierarchy. Its exploration of complex emotions and desires has become a staple in American drama, with its legacy extending to films like Tennessee Williams' own The Glass Menagerie. Moreover, the play has been recognized for its nuanced portrayal of women's lives during this period.

The 1955 version of Cat on a Hot Tin Roof won the Tony Award for Best Play that year and continues to be performed in various theatrical productions around the world, showcasing Williams' contribution to American theatre and his exploration of complex human emotions.

Their legacy is studied through the lens of historical causation.", "summary": "Cat on a Hot Tin Roof is the play by Tennessee Williams (1911–1983), which premiered on Broadway at the Morosco Theatre on 24 March 1955 (directed by Elia Kazan, with Ben Gazzara as Brick and Barbara Bel Geddes as Maggie) and won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama in 1955 — his second after A Streetcar Named Desire (1947). Set on a Mississippi Delta plantation over a single evening, the play centres on the dysfunctional Pollitt family assembled to celebrate the birthday of Big Daddy (a cotton millionaire dying of cancer), the collision between his favourite son Brick (an alcoholic ex-footballer consumed by guilt over the death of his friend Skipper and unable to consummate his marriage) and Brick's wife Maggie (the 'cat on a hot tin roof' — restless, sexually frustrated, fighting for her place in the family and the inheritance). The play's central preoccupation is with mendacity — Big Daddy's deathbed declaration that 'mendacity is the system we live in' stands as the play's moral centre — and with the denied homoerotic love between Brick and Skipper, which Williams presents as the emotional truth that none of the characters can name or acknowledge.

Cat on a Hot Tin Roof is one of the most psychologically intense dramas in the American theatrical canon, and one of the most controversial in its original production: director Elia Kazan persuaded Williams to rewrite Act III to give Big Daddy a larger role and to soften Brick's psychological resolution, producing two versions of the play (the original, which Williams preferred; and the Broadway version, which is more commonly performed). The play's frank treatment of homosexuality — even in the oblique, unspoken form in which it appears — was daring for 1955 Broadway, and the 1958 film adaptation (with Paul Newman and Elizabeth Taylor) was required to suppress the homosexual subtext entirely by the Hollywood Production Code.

Williams's three great plays — The Glass Menagerie (1944), A Streetcar Named Desire (1947), and Cat on a Hot Tin Roof (1955) — collectively established him as the preeminent poet-dramatist of the American stage, and Cat on a Hot Tin Roof's treatment of desire, denial, and the lies by which families maintain their coherence at the cost of truth is his most psychologically complex achievement.", "subjects": ["American Drama", "Contemporary Era", "Tennessee Williams", "Theatre", "20th Century", "American Literature", "Southern Literature", "Drama"], "frameworks": ["STRUCTURAL_ANALYSIS", "CAUSE_AND_EFFECT"], "historicalSignificance": {"significanceScore": 7, "significanceNarrative": "Tennessee Williams' Cat on a Hot Tin Roof has had significant regional impact, challenging societal norms and influencing feminist-influenced works in American theatre.", "significanceCategory": "regional"}, "_editLog": [{"timestamp": "2026-05-21T01:21:34Z", "editorId": "ollama/llama3.2:3b·local·manasa151-MS-7C56", "field": "summary", "oldValue": "Stage play by tennessee williams Created by Tennessee Williams.
